newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rate up on weekend covering.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rate up on weekend covering.

text.p: Manila overnight rates moved higher to an average of 14.5625 from 14.53125 percent as banks covered their three-day reserve weekend positions, traders said.
One bank dealer noted rates had persistently remained high for over a week now because banks are covering their liquidity positions until the year end.
"It will keep rates high in the next few weeks," said the same dealer. Banks are anticipating a tighthening of their liquidity positions due to the high spending during the Christmas season.
Rates jumped to a high of 16.5 percent, which traders described as off-market deals. The low was at 12.25 percent.
"Anything higher than 15 percent is off-market. These were done by small banks," said a second trader.
Traders said rates had eased before the session ended.
Market volume narrowed to 23.618 billion from 24.752 billion pesos. There were 38 lenders and 28 borrowers.
The secondary market in T-bills continued to see muted activity, traders said.
"We haven't traded. Nobody's buying. Everybody's trying to sell," said one trader.
The high overnight rates had kept banks from making positions in the secondary market, dealers said.
Dealers said three-month bills were being quoted at 11.45 to 11.60 percent; the six months at 11.90 to 12.10; and the one year at 12.50 to 12.575 percent.
